simple.meaning: עָרַב (ʻârab) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to grow dusky at sundown.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Judges, 1 Samuel, Isaiah, beginning at Judges 19:9. Its contexts include family, Torah, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָרַב (H6150).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עָרַב (ʻârab) / H6150 is traced through Judges 19:9, 1 Samuel 17:16, Isaiah 24:11 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: When the man rose up to depart, he, and his concubine, and his servant, his father-in-law, the young lady’s father, said to him, “Behold, now the day draws toward evening, please stay all night. Behold, the day is ending. Stay here, that your heart may be merry; and tomorrow go on your way early, that you may go home.”
